e.etymology: The Turkish word for deep, used there for both girls and boys. In the US the same spelling can also be a variant of Darren.
An affectionate form of Radha, from a Sanskrit root for success and prosperity. Radha is the beloved of Krishna in Hindu tradition.
A spelling of Dara, a name with more than one source: a Biblical Hebrew name and the Irish Dara, from a word for oak.
e.note: Darah is the Malay and Indonesian word for blood.

e.etymology: The French form of Latin Desiderius, from desiderium, longing. Two early French saints bore the name.
A spelling of Amina, the feminine of Arabic amin, trustworthy. The closely related Aminah was the name of the Prophet Muhammad's mother.
From Sanskrit lakshmi, a mark or sign, and so good fortune. Lakshmi is the Hindu goddess of wealth and prosperity, honored at Diwali.
namesakes: Padma Lakshmi (former host of Top Chef; surname)

assoc.t: Hindu goddess of wealth and good fortune

e.etymology: From the German surname Jaeger, the ordinary German word for a hunter.

assoc.t: Jager, bar shorthand for Jagermeister liqueur

e.note: Jager is common bar shorthand for Jagermeister, as in Jager bombs.

e.etymology: Several unrelated names. In Japanese, Hina is written with various kanji, often ones for sunlight and greens. In Urdu it is the word for henna, and in Polynesian myth Hina is a goddess linked to the moon.
Used as a short form in the Daria and Dario family of names, which go back to the Persian royal name Darius.
A respelling of Delilah, the Old Testament woman who betrayed Samson. The Hebrew name is usually read as delicate or languishing.
A Mexican name drawn from an indigenous language of western Mexico; it is usually explained as a word for corn.
A respelling of Tatum, an English surname from a place name meaning the homestead of a man called Tata.
A recent name used mainly in Mexican American families, alongside Yareli and Yaretzi. Its source is not documented.
From the Hebrew verb form ashira, I will sing, the opening word of the Song of the Sea in Exodus. A separate Hebrew word written the same way in English means wealthy.
The Yiddish form of Shlomo, the Hebrew name of King Solomon, from shalom, peace.
From Arabic dhakir, one who remembers, from the same root as dhikr, the devotional remembrance of God.
The Hebrew form of Eleazar, from El, God, and azar, helped. In the Old Testament Elazar is Aaron's son and successor as high priest.
A respelling of Malia, the Hawaiian form of Maria (Mary).
A respelling of Tatum, an English surname from a place name meaning the homestead of a man called Tata.

e.meaning: depends on the kanji; often tie or bind, or gentle
e.etymology: A Japanese name written with many kanji pairs, such as those for bind and clothing or for gentle and clothing, so the meaning depends on the characters chosen.
A name used mainly in Cuban and other Latin American families. Its source is not documented; it sits close to Biblical names such as Eliel and Eliezer.
A pet form of names that begin with Ad-, such as Addison, Adeline and Adelaide, here spelled with a final i.
For boys, a spelling of Isa, the Arabic name of Jesus as it appears in the Quran. For girls its source is less clear.
Used mainly in Spanish-speaking families. It follows the pattern of Hebrew names ending in -el, of God, such as Adiel and Eliel, but has no settled derivation.
From Hebrew avi, my father, and Yah, a short form of the divine name. It is the Hebrew form of the Biblical Abijah, borne by both men and women.
A modern spelling in the family of Aria and Araya.
A Yiddish form of Yehuda (Judah), used in Hasidic families; the Bible ties Yehuda to the Hebrew for praise. Yida is also a romanized Chinese given name.
A pet form of Jordan, from the River Jordan, whose Hebrew name Yarden comes from a verb meaning to descend or flow down.
The Scandinavian spelling of Alaric, from a Germanic name read as ruler of all. Alaric I was the Visigoth king who sacked Rome in 410.

e.meaning: Roman god of trade and messengers
e.etymology: From Latin Mercurius, the Roman god of commerce and messenger of the gods, whose name is related to merx, merchandise. The planet and the metal are named for him.

assoc.t: Freddie Mercury, lead singer of Queen
toxic liquid metal once used in thermometers
Mercury outboard boat motors; Ford's former Mercury cars

e.etymology: For girls, a Japanese name whose meaning depends on the kanji chosen. As a man's name in Estonia, Finland and German-speaking countries, Juri is a form of George by way of Russian Yuri.
e.note: Sounds the same as the English word jury.

assoc.t: Juri, a fighter in the Street Fighter games
